messages:
Maria: Heads-up — bringing up model v2.3-quant on canary and seeing a consistent drop in longform MRR for the docs cohort (~4.6% relative). Not a huge perf change, but it's outside our soft threshold. Anyone else seeing the same?
Aj: I saw that too in the daily run. baseline v2.2 -> v2.3-quant. latency p95 improved ~30ms, cost down ~18%, but MRR drop is worrying. do we have slice breakdowns?
Liam: Quick numbers from the smoke: docs_cohort MRR 0.841 -> 0.803, longctx recall down slightly. hallucination sigs not elevated in the basic checks.
Maria: Uploaded the per-slice CSV to the run artifacts (link) and a quick plot. main hit is the >1500 token slice.
EvalBot: smoke-check results: quality-regression: true, delta=4.6%, significance p=0.02, n=2.1k samples. latency_p95: -30ms.
Sam: Can we isolate whether quantization is causing context truncation or tokenization mismatch? any prefix mismatch reported?
Ryan: I ran a kv-warmup trace — kv cache hit-rate is fine. token-prefix mismatch appears in ~0.4% of longctx examples (might be noise).
Aj: Proposal: hold traffic at 2% and run a targeted AB focused only on long-doc cohort with 10k samples. If signal persists we should trigger auto-fallback.
Maria: Agreed. Also want to try a hybrid quant profile (int8 for MLP, int4 attention) to see if fidelity recovers.
Liam: Quick suggestion for canary config if we want auto-fallback:
```
canary_policy:
  initial_traffic: 2%
  escalate: [5%, 15%]
  hold_if:
    mrr_drop_relative: 0.02   # 2% relative drop triggers hold
    p_value_threshold: 0.05
  auto_fallback:
    enabled: true
    rollback_if_mrr_drop: 0.03  # 3% absolute relative
    max_wait_minutes: 60
```
Sam: That rollback_if_mrr_drop looks strict but reasonable given we're touching longform. Could we instead use an ensemble check (compare outputs with v2.2 baseline) and only auto-fallback if ensemble disagreement + metric drop?
Maria: Yes — add ensemble_concordance < 0.92 as an additional gate. we saw a few examples where wording shifted but exact match stayed similar.
Ryan: Running the 10k AB now on the long-doc slice. ETA ~45m. I'll post interim diagnostics here.
EvalBot: queued: ab_test_1722223333_longdocs (10k). will report aggregated metrics every 15m.
Aj: One more ask — add a focused canonical prompt set for legal/PII-heavy docs to ensure safety signal unchanged. we don't want subtle regressions there.
Maria: Done — included the safety sub-slice in AB.
Liam: If AB shows persistent delta >2.5% after 10k samples and p<0.05, recommend immediate rollback to v2.2 and follow-up with quantization gradient sweep.
Maria: Thanks — leave the canary traffic locked at 2% until we have AB verdict. tagging @oncall if auto-fallback triggers. :eyes:
Ryan: interim stats: 3k samples in, MRR delta 4.3%, p=0.03, ensemble_concordance=0.89. leaning towards rollback.
Sam: sounds like consensus. Maria, do we want a soft-rollback (route new sessions to v2.2 but let sticky older sessions finish) or hard rollback?
Maria: Soft-rollback preferred to avoid in-flight inconsistencies. open a rollback runbook and I'll initiate.
EvalBot: ab_test_1722223333_longdocs update: final n=10,004; mrr_delta=4.57% (v2.3-quant worse), p=0.012, concordance=0.90. trigger conditions met.
Maria: Initiating soft rollback now. rolling route weight -> v2.2 for new sessions. filing postmortem with follow-up quant sweep plan.
Aj: Postmortem checklist: compare per-layer quant noise, run hybrid quant profile, re-run with longer burn-in for KV, and extend canonical prompts for more coverage.
Liam: I'll take the quant sweep. Sam, can you own the postmortem doc?
Sam: Yep — I'll draft it and include sample diffs + failing examples.
Maria: Thanks everyone. keeping this channel as the canonical thread. we'll re-open canary after fixes and a dedicated regression run. :thumbsup:
